newsitem.title: USA: Key senator voices qualms on Clinton's CIA choice.
newsitem.headline: Key senator voices qualms on Clinton's CIA choice.

text.p: The chairman of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence said Wednesday he had "great reservations" about confirming Anthony Lake, President Clinton's choice to become the next director of central intelligence.

"I have great reservations about Mr Lake and about his sensitivity," Senator Arlen Specter, a Pennsylvania Republican, said, citing Lake's role in a covert diplomatic policy that cut Congress and the CIA out of the loop on the transshipment of Iranian arms to Bosnia.
As Clinton's national security adviser, Lake was an architect of a secret policy that encouraged Croatia to help ship arms to Bosnian Muslims in 1994 in violation of a United Nations embargo.
Specter said he would vote against confirmation if Lake maintained that as Central Intelligence Agency director he could withhold such secrets from the intelligence oversight panels.
"It would make it an easy question for me to vote no on his confirmation," Specter said at a farewell hearing for the outgoing CIA director, John Deutch.
